chapter: New Orleans musicians, recordings and radio
title: King Oliver, the soft-playing one-eyed trumpeter
summary: Oliver was big, had one eye, and could play so softly it could not be heard across the room; he and Louis together made beautiful music.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah, let's talk about some of the people. We were talking -- we were mentioning before King Oliver, for instance, whom you worked with --
Oh, he was fine. He was a great big man, not what you'd call fat, but big, tall and healthy looking, you know. And he had one eye. He had one eye.
He had one eye? I didn't know that.
Yeah, he had one eye. And he played the sweetest trumpet. He did -- you know what he could do,
Chris? He could play his trumpet here, and you could be standing over there at that door and couldn't hear him --

-- if he wanted to -- he played that soft -- if he wanted to. And so sweet and beautiful. And he played that thing, Jerusalem, Jerusalem, sing for the night is over. He played the lead, and somebody else would play the other part of it, you know. It would be three or four of them playing. And what a beautiful thing it would be. You know?
And so would -- and some -- when Louie was there, then he -- just he and Louie would play, and it would be the most beautiful thing you ever heard in your life.
